title: Derived evaluation with two targets of finite injective dimension
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K,L,M\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use $R\operatorname{Hom}_R$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site and $\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}$ computed by a K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex] followed by the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Suppose (i) $L$ and $M$ are each isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $R$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; (ii) $T=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)$ has finite Tor dimension, meaning there are integers $a\leq b$ such that for every $R$-module $N$, $H^j(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0])=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$; and (iii) every good truncation $\tau_{\leq n}K$ (cohomology $H^j(K)$ for $j\leq n$ and zero otherwise) is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Then the canonical derived evaluation morphism $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L),M)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $K,L,M$. The morphism is the transpose of evaluation followed by composition: $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\to M$, pairing the first and third factors into $L$ and then evaluating into $M$, with the usual graded symmetries.

proof.text: Write $F(A)=T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$ and $G(A)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,L),M)$. By [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map], these are exact functors and the evaluation-and-composition map $e_A:F(A)\to G(A)$ is a natural transformation compatible with shifts and distinguished triangles. This is exactly the map specified in the statement.

source.place: Tags 0A67 and 0A60; Tag 0A69 uses this map throughout

proof.text: Choose bounded injective representatives $J,I$ for $L,M$ and fixed integers $u,v$ with $J^r=0$ for $r>u$ and $I^r=0$ for $r<v$. Thus $L$ is bounded below. For each $n$, use the standard truncation triangle $A_n=\tau_{\le n}K\xrightarrow{i_n}K\to E_n=\tau_{\ge n+1}K\to A_n[1]$; the tail has a representative $B_n$ zero below $n+1$. These are the truncation triangle and representative characterization of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] (1) and [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category].

Hypothesis (iii) says $A_n$ is pseudo-coherent for every $n$. Apply [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-pseudocoherent] with $K=A_n$, the bounded-below object $L$ of Step 2 and the finite-injective-dimension object $M$ of hypothesis (i). Thus $e_{A_n}$ is an isomorphism for every $n$.

Fix the Tor interval $[a,b]$ of $T$ from (ii). Apply [lem-sc-source-tor-amplitude-lower-tensor-bound] in $R$-modules to $T$ and $E_n$: its conclusion is $H^r(F(E_n))=0$ for $r<n+1+a$. Apply [lem-trf-double-derived-hom-lower-bound] with $q=n+1$ and the fixed models $J,I$: it gives $H^r(G(E_n))=0$ for $r<n+1+v-u$. Thus $c=\max(-a,u-v)$ is independent of $n$ and both tails vanish in every degree $r\le n-c$.

source.place: Tag 0A69, the two tail objects and their uniform vanishing.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-exact-comparison-connective-approximations] to $F,G,e$, the triangles of Step 2, the truncated isomorphisms of Step 3, and the single constant $c$ of Step 4. It yields that $e_K$ is an isomorphism. This is the canonical evaluation morphism of Step 1; its naturality in all three variables is already part of [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map], independent of the choices of $J,I,n$.
